places.name: Andalen Plantation

why.founding: A Dres saltrice enterprise with a great house, a drying floor, a counting room and a labour row, abandoned at the secession when the people who worked it stopped and the family who owned it did not come back.
why.siteAdvantages: Prime saltrice ground on slack water with a private landing — everything an agricultural enterprise needs, and it still failed, which is the point.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies the house. The fields are worked by the people from the rows down the road, who take the crop and will not enter the buildings.
why.pressures: The house is intact and unlooted, which after two centuries means somebody is maintaining an arrangement rather than a building; nobody will say who.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be occupied within a month if the field-holders ever decided the taboo was over, and the house is worth more than the whole village.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in the ex-Imperial agricultural belt
hardConstraints: prime saltrice ground with a private landing
preferences: a great house, drying floor, counting room and labour row

notableNpcSlots: the field-holder who takes the crop and will not go in

vibe.silhouette: A two-storey Dunmer great house with a colonnaded drying floor beside it, standing whole and shuttered in the middle of worked fields.

vibe.materials: Cut basalt and Dunmer joinery, entirely unaltered — the one building in the north that no Argonian hand has touched.
vibe.signatureFeature: It is unlooted. Two hundred years, no roof failure, no broken shutter, and the fields farmed to the doorstep.
vibe.condition: Impossibly good, which is what makes it frightening.
vibe.mood: Avoided rather than haunted, and the distinction matters to everyone here.
vibe.approach: You walk through worked fields towards a shut house, and nobody working the fields looks up.
vibe.senses: Crop noise on all sides and, at the walls, an absence of it.

the counting room: the records of who was owned here

places.name: Bogmother

why.founding: An ancient sacred site south-west of Stormhold, ruined for centuries and never abandoned, holding relics venerable enough that nobody moved them.
why.siteAdvantages: At the far end of a stone causeway from Stormhold — the causeway exists because the site does, not the other way round.
why.occupantsMotive: A caretaker few keep it swept and the relics in place; the city funds them because being seen not to would be intolerable.
why.pressures: Crocodiles have moved inside the town threshold and the caretakers have decided not to remove them.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be robbed within a season if the caretakers left, and the city would blame itself for centuries.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: a landmark for its whole district; a village within 1 km tends it
hardConstraints: at the end of a stone causeway

notableNpcSlots: the eldest caretaker, who feeds the crocodiles

vibe.silhouette: Terraced stone half-sunk in bog, swept clean above the waterline and green below it, with wide flooded courts.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, black water, the caretakers' white cloth, and green to the exact height of the flood.
vibe.materials: Ancient Argonian terrace stone; the caretakers add nothing but brooms, cloth and offerings.
vibe.signatureFeature: The relics, still in place in an open chamber, in a ruin with no door.
vibe.condition: Ruined for centuries and immaculately maintained as a ruin — a distinction the caretakers will explain.
vibe.mood: Holy, patient, quietly dangerous at ankle height.
vibe.approach: The causeway runs at it straight over open bog; you see the terraces for the last four hundred metres.
vibe.senses: Brooms; water displaced by something large; no birds inside the walls.

provisions: the sacred ruin at the causeway's end

places.name: Boom-Keeper's Lodge

why.founding: The monsoon boom across the northern channel has to be opened and closed by somebody, and that somebody has to live within a horn's call of it, so the lodge exists as a condition of the boom's contract.
why.siteAdvantages: The one firm bank within two hundred metres of the boom's anchor, high enough that the keeper is not flooded out of the job.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper is paid in a share of the tolls the boom makes possible, which is a good living in a wet year and nothing at all in a dry one.
why.pressures: The contract is with a Stormhold office that has not sent an inspector in eleven years; the keeper has quietly begun charging boats directly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned the day the boom was replaced with a fixed barrier, which is exactly what the vicecanons keep proposing.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: always paired with a crossing, landing or light
hardConstraints: within a horn's call of the boom anchor

notableNpcSlots: the keeper who has started charging boats on his own account

vibe.palette: Tarred black timber, green channel water, and the brass gleam of a horn that is polished daily because it is the job.
vibe.materials: Heavier timber than a village house — this is infrastructure's dwelling, built to the boom's standard, not the marsh's.
vibe.signatureFeature: The horn: a brass channel-horn on the gable, and the keeper's whole authority is that everyone downstream knows what it means.
vibe.condition: Solid, isolated, over-built for one person.
vibe.mood: Self-important in an entirely earned way.
vibe.approach: The boom reads first as a line on the water; the lodge is the small thing at one end of it.
vibe.senses: A winch pawl; water piling against timber; one horn note, rarely, carrying a long way.

boom shut (and a horn nobody is answering)

places.name: Branchmont

why.occupantsMotive: The villagers work it as their own; three separate claimants say otherwise, and one of them is Dunmer.
why.pressures: The dispute is in Thorn's title court and has been for eleven years, which suits the villagers perfectly.

places.name: Breathes-Underneath

why.founding: A flooded chamber under the Loriasel shelf with air trapped in its crown — reachable only by a twelve-metre dive through a slot, and containing, as far as anyone can establish, nothing.
why.siteAdvantages: A limestone void that never drained, sealed by its own roof, with the only opening below water.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The divers' landing knows about it and treats it as a test rather than a resource.
why.pressures: The air in it is old and the divers argue about how many breaths it is good for; two people have found out and one came back.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become genuinely dangerous rather than merely frightening if the slot silted, and the channel above it is silting.

notableNpcSlots: the diver who came back, and will not discuss the one who did not

vibe.palette: Black water, and the mercury-bright underside of the air pocket, which is the only light-coloured thing down here.
vibe.materials: Bare wet limestone, no worked surface anywhere, which is itself the point — this is not a ruin.
vibe.signatureFeature: The surfacing: you come up inside solid rock into a metre of air that has been there longer than the province has had a name.
vibe.condition: Geological, unchanged, indifferent.
vibe.mood: Awe with an edge of panic.
vibe.approach: There is no approach. There is a marked slot on the shelf and a decision.

slot silting (a tighter squeeze and a real decision)

places.name: Buried Blades

why.founding: In 1E 2836 the Argonians stopped fighting the Blackwater War overnight, and in the north that decision was made physical: an entire district's weapons were oiled, wrapped and buried in one pit, deliberately, so that stopping could not be easily undone.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry gravel lens under a low rise — chosen because it drains, which is why the contents are still there and still recognisable.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody guards it. Four villages know where it is and have known for sixteen hundred years, and the knowledge is transmitted as a warning rather than as an asset.
why.pressures: An-Xileel interest in the province's armament has made the pit's existence newly awkward, and one of the four villages has started asking what the others would do.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would change the north's politics in a week if it were opened, which is the reason four villages have not opened it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a battlefield or a village of the period
hardConstraints: a dry gravel lens under a rise

notableNpcSlots: the village elder who has started asking the other three

vibe.silhouette: A low grassed rise with a single upright stone at one end and no other feature for four hundred metres.
vibe.palette: Grass over gravel, one grey upright, and, if the turf is cut, the astonishing black-and-oil-brown of wrapped iron.
vibe.materials: The pit is lined with clay and the bundles are wrapped in oiled hide — a burial done with enormous care by people who meant it.
vibe.signatureFeature: The care: this is not a hiding place, it is a burial, and the difference is visible the moment anything is uncovered.
vibe.condition: Undisturbed, and in far better condition than sixteen centuries should allow.
vibe.approach: It is a rise on a plain. There is nothing to see, which is the entire design.
vibe.senses: Nothing. Four villages' worth of silence about one field.

provisions: a district's worth of weapons, buried on purpose, that the An-Xileel would like
a four-village secret with one member wavering

localStateVariants: buried
opened (and four villages' arrangement over)

places.name: Channel Cross

why.founding: Where two navigable channels cross, everything stops, so a village stands on the crossing itself.
why.siteAdvantages: The junction of the trunk channel and the Bogmother feeder — every boat in the district passes through it.
why.occupantsMotive: It lives on pilotage: the channels braid and only local people know which arm is open this season.
why.pressures: The pilots have begun charging by the season rather than the trip, which the boat crews call a toll.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be irrelevant if anyone ever dredged and marked the braids properly.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed

preferences: a pilot's platform with sightlines up both channels

occupants: D2 crews waiting on a pilot

vibe.silhouette: A tall pilot's platform at the middle of a water crossroads, with the village built outward from it in four arms.
vibe.palette: Black water in four directions, reed roofs, and one raised platform with a lamp on it.
vibe.materials: Stilt construction with one deliberately over-tall structure — the only vertical in the district.
vibe.signatureFeature: The pilot platform: high enough to see up all four channels, which is the whole reason the village exists.
vibe.condition: Sound; the platform is the best-maintained thing for kilometres.
vibe.approach: The platform lamp is visible up all four channels at night, which is the province's cue language working properly.
vibe.senses: Water from four directions; a horn used to call pilots; poles.

places.name: Climbs-To-See
sources: world/sources/sites/candidate-sites.md (no long sightlines below the rim)

why.founding: The north marsh has no rises and no sightlines, so the villages built one: a stack of platforms up a stand of trees, high enough to see the flood coming a day before it arrives.
why.siteAdvantages: Three trunks close enough to brace against each other, on root mat firm enough to take the base frame.
why.occupantsMotive: A flood-watcher through the wet season, paid by four villages; out of season, anyone who wants the view.
why.pressures: The bracing between trunks is the weak point and the trees move independently in wind; two platforms have been rebuilt after storms in a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned if one of the three trunks came down, because two will not brace.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: placed where a viewshed pass shows a dead zone
hardConstraints: three braceable trunks on firm root mat

occupants: D3 in the canopy out of it
notableNpcSlots: the flood-watcher who calls the day the water turns

vibe.silhouette: A lattice of platforms climbing three trunks, tapering as it rises, with a small railed cage at the top above the leaves.
vibe.palette: Green-black below, and above the leaf line an abrupt world of grey sky and silver water to the horizon.
vibe.materials: Lashed frames braced between three living trunks, with a rope hoist for anything heavier than a person.
vibe.signatureFeature: The transition: eleven metres of enclosed green, then a hatch, then the entire north marsh laid out flat.
vibe.condition: Rebuilt in patches; the top cage is the newest thing on it.
vibe.approach: Nothing about it reads from the ground until you are under it and looking up.
vibe.senses: Creak and sway; insects loud below, wind alone above; the hoist rope running.

places.name: Crystalgate

why.founding: Stormhold's crystal has to be cut, graded and sold somewhere that is not the city, because the city taxes what passes its gates.

why.occupantsMotive: The cutting houses are guild-like and hereditary; the town exists entirely downstream of one skill.
why.pressures: The vicecanons want the cutting inside the walls and have tried tariffs twice.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse into a road village the day the Silyanorn seams ran out — which the diggers say is a generation away.

places.name: Cut-And-Stack

why.founding: The north's only fuel that is not carried: peat banks cut in the dry months and stacked to dry, worked by three villages that have no timber worth burning.
why.siteAdvantages: A raised bog on the plain edge, deep enough to cut for three generations and dry enough to stack on.
why.occupantsMotive: Fuel, and the fact that a stack of turves is the closest thing a village here has to money in a bank.
why.pressures: The cut face is a wall of exposed peat that catches in a dry year and then burns underground for months, which has happened twice and is why the villages now cut in strips.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned as too dangerous if a fire ever reached a stack rather than a face.

vibe.palette: Peat brown-black, stack shadow, and the pale straw of the cut-strip boundaries.
vibe.materials: Turves and nothing else — the only structure here is made of the material being extracted.
vibe.signatureFeature: The strips: the cut is broken into strips with unworked baulks between, and the baulks are firebreaks that exist because of two bad years.

places.name: Cut-In-The-Wall

why.founding: The Stormhold ravine system has more wall than floor, and the households the terraced city could not house cut their own dwellings into a side ravine's face — outside the city's walls, and outside its rents.
why.siteAdvantages: A soft band in the ravine wall, easy to cut and above the wet-season torrent, with the city's lights visible round the bend.
why.occupantsMotive: Rent. There is none here, and that fact organises the whole community, which describes itself as a neighbourhood and is described by the vicecanons as an encroachment.
why.pressures: The vicecanons have twice sent surveyors to establish whether the cuttings are within the city's boundary; both surveyors were treated hospitably and both reports were inconclusive.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be inside the city, and paying, within a year of a survey that came back conclusive.

the vicecanons' surveyor, well fed and still uncertain

places.name: Draws-The-Herds

why.founding: When the northern floodplain dries, every animal on it walks to the same three tree-islands for water, and for two months this ground holds more meat, more predators and more people than anywhere else in the region.
why.siteAdvantages: The last standing water on the plain: three spring-fed pools under tree cover that do not fail in a normal dry year.
why.occupantsMotive: Four villages hunt it under an allocation they renegotiate every year at Wolk Market, and the negotiation is the region's real political calendar.
why.pressures: A long dry year concentrates everything harder and the allocation stops holding; the last time it failed, two villages did not speak for a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end the villages' year as they organise it if the springs failed, which is the thing the north actually fears.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: the last water in a drying landscape
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the region's ecological engine; villages time their year on it
hardConstraints: spring-fed pools that survive the dry season

occupants: D1 hunters from four villages, in season
nothing at all, ten months a year
notableNpcSlots: the allocation-keeper who reads out last year's shares
the hunter who takes more than his village's line

places.name: Dry-Under-Water

why.founding: Stormhold's crystal trade comes out of a Barsaebic Ayleid undercity that the city has been quarrying for centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: The ravine walls below the city expose the Ayleid galleries directly — the diggings are the ruin, entered sideways.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanons license the diggings because the crystal pays for the border offices; the diggers dig because the Owing says so.
why.pressures: Every season takes more of an Ayleid structure that the Synod would pay handsomely to study intact.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be closed by any authority that valued the ruin above the revenue, which is no authority the north has.

places.name: Sings-For-The-Pipes
sources: world/sources/lore/regions/waters.md (the Panther's frogs and the vossa-satl)

why.founding: The Panther basin's frogs have the chirp the vossa-satl copies, and somebody worked out three generations ago that the tone breeds true, so this is a farm that culls by ear.
why.siteAdvantages: Six spring-fed ponds at slightly different temperatures, which is what lets the farm hold six different tones on one site.
why.occupantsMotive: The pipe-makers of Thorn and Stormhold pay by tone, and a matched set of six is worth more than the ponds that made it.
why.pressures: The tone drifts if the pond temperature drifts, so the farm's whole craft is water management dressed up as animal husbandry; a hot year ruins a decade of selection.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose its stock in one season to a spring failure, and the selection could not be redone in under thirty years.

vibe.approach: You hear it long before you see it, and what you hear is six chords that do not belong together.

places.name: Sits-Above-The-Flood

why.founding: Six houses on the only rise for a kilometre of the Stormhold flood plain — the hamlet has no other reason to exist and has never pretended otherwise.
why.siteAdvantages: A gravel rise two metres above the plain, dry in every flood anyone has recorded, on the line villages walk between the terraces and the north road.
why.occupantsMotive: They farm the plain and sleep on the rise; in flood season they farm nothing and take in everyone whose ground is under water, at a price.
why.pressures: The rise is finite and the flood is not; two of the six houses now stand on made ground the households carried up themselves, basket by basket.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would double in size and halve in dryness if the flood took the next rise downstream, which it is visibly working on.

places.name: Stands-On-The-Island

why.founding: A tree-island in the north marsh with real ground on it — an acre of soil that is never under water — and therefore a village, because in this landscape that is the whole argument.
why.siteAdvantages: Ringed by water on every side, so nothing walks in; the ground is dry enough to bury in and to grow on, which no floating village can say.
why.occupantsMotive: They own the only permanent ground for two kilometres and rent standing room on it during the flood, a business the whole marsh resents and uses.
why.pressures: The island is not getting bigger and the flood season is getting longer; the crown terrace is filling faster than the ground below it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would have to stop burying its dead in the soil — the argument currently splitting the village.

places.name: Stillrise Village

why.founding: A village that took a Daedric bargain to survive the Knahaten Flu and has been technically dead ever since, sustained by a soul-gem array.
why.siteAdvantages: West of Stormhold on ground the Flu emptied around them — they are the only thing left on it.
why.occupantsMotive: They maintain the illusions because the alternative is to stop; three and a half centuries of infighting has settled nothing.
why.pressures: The array was preserved rather than destroyed in 2E 582, so the argument that started then is still running, with the same participants — who are technically dead, held in the world by Clavicus Vile's bargain, which is why the argument cannot simply outlive them.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end the day someone broke the array — and half the village would thank them.

places.name: Stormhold

why.founding: Built on ravine-severed mounds above a waterfall, over a Barsaebic Ayleid crystal undercity the city has never stopped mining.
why.siteAdvantages: The head of navigation on the northern river: everything from Morrowind stops here, and the ravines make each mound its own defensible quarter.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanons — plural, and rivals — run the state's only working border offices because the river trade pays for offices.
why.pressures: The Knahaten Flu began here, and the city has never been allowed to forget it; the Silyanorn tunnels below are worked by people with no other option.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose its purpose if the Morrowind trade failed, and its shape if the waterfall ever cut back past the first mound.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: astride a navigable river above the falls
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the northern hinge: Tenmar Wall east, Bogmother south-west, the Morrowind road north
preferences: an undercity entrance inside the walls

vibe.palette: Wet grey terrace stone, white water, dark ravine, and crystal-blue points in the undercity mouths at night.

places.name: Bogmother Causeway

why.founding: Stormhold built a stone causeway to Bogmother because the pilgrimage could not wait on the season.
why.siteAdvantages: The shortest line of shallow bog between the city's south gate and the sacred ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The city maintains it as a civic duty; the maintenance gang is a hereditary office with a bad reputation.
why.pressures: It is stone, which post-Duskfall is a moral compromise — and it is the only reason the compromise is tolerated.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced with timber if it ever failed completely, which the caretakers would prefer and the city would not.

vibe.palette: Grey stone, brown bog, and a very large amount of sky for this province.
vibe.materials: Cut stone slabs on a rubble core — the largest single piece of stone construction the north has built since the Duskfall.

vibe.condition: Continuously repaired and continuously sinking.
vibe.approach: It goes flat to the horizon out of the city's south gate, which is the only straight line for kilometres.
vibe.senses: Feet on stone — an unfamiliar sound here; bog gas; wind with nothing to break it.

places.name: Tear Road Stage

why.founding: The Tear road is one of the province's two canon exit roads, and a road to Morrowind needs a last stage on the Argonian side.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the road leaves the marsh for the pass — the last place with fodder, water and level ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The stage is run by a family who take payment in both coin and salt and prefer salt.
why.pressures: Dunmer caravans and Argonian porters use the same yard and keep to opposite sides of it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a border town if the traffic doubled, and everyone here can name the year they think that will happen.

places.name: Tearmouth

why.founding: Where the north river meets navigable water, cargo has to change hulls; a two-culture port grew at the transfer point, Argonian on the water and Dunmer on the bank, and has been arguing about which half is the port ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: The head of deep-draught navigation: below it a keeled hull can float, above it only shallow craft, and no engineering has ever changed that.
why.occupantsMotive: Transfer fees, warehousing, a customs presence run out of Stormhold with two clerks, and a great deal of business that the two clerks are not shown.
why.pressures: Both halves of the town want the customs house on the other side of the water; the Thorn road wants a bridge; and the whole place empties for six weeks when the river runs too hard to transfer at all.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose half its trade to a deeper channel and all of it to a bridge, and has resisted both for a century.

places.name: Ten-Maur-Wolk
aliases: Tenmar Wall (the Imperial exonym; the Third Empire's maps renamed the site)

why.founding: A temple to Boethiah and Vaermina raised by Dunmer dissidents who fled the Tribunal, and abandoned by them. The Third Empire's surveyors renamed it Tenmar Wall on their maps; the north never adopted the name, and the market town that grew at the junction beside it is a separate, later thing.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the junction where the roads from Helstrom, Stormhold and Alten Corimont meet, which is why everyone knows it and nobody enters it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The marker posts around it are maintained, which is the loudest thing about the place.
why.pressures: The market town next door lives off the junction and pretends the ruin is scenery; the second atrocity on this ground is the Dres slave road that ran past it, not anything the dissidents built.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would draw a cult within a year if the markers ever stopped being renewed.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: deliberately avoided by every route
preferences: dissident-built outbuildings, Dunmer-cut and long empty
the Dres road passing within sight

vibe.silhouette: A black stone shrine in a clearing, ringed at forty metres by white-painted posts that are obviously new.
vibe.palette: Black stone, white posts, and grass that is a different green inside the ring.
vibe.materials: Daedric black basalt; the outbuildings beside it are ordinary Dunmer-cut stone, dissidents' work, and far more legible than the shrine.
vibe.signatureFeature: The marker ring: repainted annually by a town that will not say who does it.
vibe.condition: Intact. Nothing here has fallen down, which for a two-thousand-year-old ruin is the tell.
vibe.approach: You can see it from the junction — it is deliberately not hidden, and that is the point.
vibe.senses: Nothing inside the ring; ordinary marsh noise outside it, which makes the contrast.

places.name: Ten-Thousand-Nests

why.founding: A stand of dead trees in shallow water where the north's wading birds nest in numbers that make the stand uninhabitable and the ground beneath it the richest fertiliser source in the region.
why.siteAdvantages: Dead standing timber over water: no predator route in, no need for the birds to leave, and forty years of guano under it.
why.occupantsMotive: The villages take guano for the terraces in one licensed month and stay away for eleven, an arrangement enforced by the smell as much as by anyone.
why.pressures: The saltrice growers want more than one month; the villages that eat the eggs want none at all; the stand itself is rotting and falling tree by tree.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would relocate entirely — birds do — if the stand came down, and nobody knows where to.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: worked seasonally from a nearby settlement

occupants: D3 in the water below the stand
notableNpcSlots: the guano licensor who is bribed annually
the egg-taker who works it out of season

vibe.palette: Guano white on everything, black water, and the grey-brown churn of ten thousand birds.

vibe.senses: A continuous roar of birds; ammonia; the specific slap of a trunk going over.

places.name: Ash Holding

why.founding: Dres families displaced by the Red Year settled the Argonian side of the pass, on land that was cheap because it had been theirs by force before.

why.occupantsMotive: They stay because Morrowind has nothing left for them; they hold themselves apart because the alternative is admitting that.
why.pressures: Every Argonian household within a day of them is descended from someone this family's ancestors owned.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would leave in a generation if the border ever hardened, and would take the herds.

why.occupantsMotive: They camp for the season and take what passes; this is not banditry as the road understands it.
why.pressures: Thorn's levy sweeps the section twice a year and finds an empty camp both times.

places.name: The Drowned Terrace

why.founding: A xanmeer whose ground subsided into the lake, taking a complete Merethic building down with it intact.

vibe.senses: Underwater silence; your own breath held; stone under your hands.

places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 255 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, submerged, danger.

places.name: Empty Socket

why.founding: A small Barsaebic structure built around a single stone socket, with the stone gone — taken, by the record cut beside it, in the same generation the building went up.

why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives here. The chamber has been searched exhaustively and there is nothing in it but the socket and the record.
why.pressures: The record beside the socket is legible and says who took the stone, and that name appears nowhere else in any source anyone has consulted.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the most important room in the north if the stone were ever put back, which is exactly the kind of sentence the Whispers scholars enjoy.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: one of a set; the set is the puzzle
hardConstraints: a rock knoll above the flood

vibe.palette: Pale block outside, and inside a green half-light off wet stone with one black square where the socket is.
vibe.materials: Barsaebic block work, single-chamber, unornamented — built for one purpose and no other.

vibe.mood: A locked room with the lock missing.
vibe.approach: The dome shows above the scrub from one direction only.
vibe.senses: Water dripping in a small hard room; nothing else at all.

places.name: Field-Edge Hearth

why.founding: The obligation applies in field country too, and in field country the comers are mostly people who have just lost an Owing case.

why.pressures: The field-owners regard it as a shelter for runaways and have said so; the villages have declined to discuss it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a flashpoint the first time an overseer took someone out of it.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: at a crossing or a road

places.name: First-Counted

why.founding: The first ground the Flu filled, in the first season, before anyone understood what was happening.
why.siteAdvantages: On the terrace below Stormhold's south gate, because at the time nobody could carry the dead further.

why.pressures: Kothringi dead are buried here alongside Argonian dead — a mixing that neither people's rite permits and both accepted.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the north's central memorial if the city could bear to make it one.

vibe.materials: Grave-stakes and cairns in the same ground, neither adapted to the other.

vibe.approach: It is the first thing you pass leaving the south gate and the last thing anyone will discuss.
vibe.senses: The city above; stakes knocking; nothing else.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 194 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

places.name: Fish Boon Ground

why.founding: Hissmir's Fish Boon Feast needs somewhere to happen that is not the pilgrimage xanmeer, and this river flat below the village has been that place for as long as the feast has existed.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide gravel flat where the river slows: shallow enough to net from the bank, wide enough for the whole village and its pilgrims, and scoured clean by every flood.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here and nothing is built here, because the flood takes it annually and that is understood to be part of the arrangement.
why.pressures: The pilgrim numbers have grown past what the flat can feed, and the Root Stewards will not turn anyone away, so the feast now runs three days instead of one.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move upstream if the river shifted its channel, which it does about once a century and is due.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: serves a settlement cluster
hardConstraints: a gravel flat on slow water below Hissmir

occupants: in season: the village, its pilgrims, and more of both than there should be
notableNpcSlots: the Root Steward who will not turn a comer away
the netter who says the run is smaller every year

vibe.palette: Wet grey shingle, brown river, and in season a long line of fires and a great deal of silver on the stones.
vibe.materials: Nothing permanent but the weir footing; everything else is brought down from the village and taken back up.

provisions: the Fish Boon Feast as a place and a date — a scene the calendar delivers
a pilgrim crowd that has outgrown its ground

places.name: The Flu Cordon

why.founding: The Flu began at Stormhold, and the north cordoned itself against its own city — the only such line drawn from the inside out.
why.siteAdvantages: A ring of markers at a day's walk from the city, following the ground where the channels make a natural boundary.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it. Nobody has crossed a marker on foot in three hundred years without noticing they did it.
why.pressures: Stormhold has never formally acknowledged that the line was drawn against Stormhold.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a diplomatic incident if anyone re-marked it, which is why nobody has.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: uses water as part of the line where it can
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: encircles a plague-abandoned village or a cairn field

vibe.palette: Lichen grey, marsh green, nothing else.
vibe.materials: Undressed set stone — the same grammar as every cordon in the province, and the only one pointing inward.
vibe.signatureFeature: The orientation: every marker faces out from Stormhold, which tells you who was being kept in.
vibe.condition: Fallen in places, never re-set, never removed.
vibe.mood: Accusatory, patient, entirely silent about it.
vibe.approach: You cross it on the Tear road without noticing and then see the next stone.
vibe.senses: Wind; the road; a long absence of anything else.

places.name: The Freed Rows

places.name: Gravel Six

why.founding: A second rise, half a day north, settled two generations later by the overflow from the first — the two hamlets are related, competitive, and consider each other's flood arrangements inadequate.
why.siteAdvantages: A longer, lower rise than its neighbour's, which means more ground and less margin — a trade the founders made knowingly.
why.occupantsMotive: Saltrice on the plain and a ferry-rope across the channel that only pays in the wet months, which is when they need it.
why.pressures: In a bad year the rise goes under by a hand's depth and the hamlet moves bodily to its rival's rise for three weeks, which neither party enjoys.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would abandon the rise permanently after two consecutive bad years, and everyone has been counting since the last one.

occupants: D2 the channel in the wet months
notableNpcSlots: the ferry-rope keeper who charges by the season, not the crossing

vibe.palette: Saltrice green in season, silt grey out of it, and the black tarred post of the ferry rope.

places.name: Guar Ground

why.founding: A second, smaller drying ground on the Thorn side, where the Dunmer holdings drive their guar in the dry months because the saltrice ground has nothing on it then.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow basin that holds a skin of water two months longer than the plain around it, with hard edges to hold a herd against.
why.occupantsMotive: Two Dunmer holdings and one Argonian village use it in rotation, which was a Dres arrangement and is now nobody's, and works anyway.

why.wouldChangeIf: Would break the rotation the first year a holding brought more guar than the basin can water, which one of them is visibly building towards.

hard edges to hold a herd

places.name: High Wrappings

why.founding: The second island's crown terrace, older and smaller than its neighbour's, and the reason its people will not accept charity from the first: their dead are already up, and have been longer.

why.pressures: The porters and the boat crews price against each other twice a day, in public, loudly.

notableNpcSlots: the landing-holder who sets the carry rate

places.name: Lightning Yard

why.founding: A second wamasu works on the northern channel, taking what the Charge Works cannot handle and specialising in the organ lanterns rather than the hide — a split that happened because two brothers stopped speaking.
why.siteAdvantages: A channel bank with running water for the flushing and a rock face to work against, far enough from the first works that the smell of the two does not combine.
why.occupantsMotive: Lanterns: the luminescent organs keep for a season if they are handled right, and this yard handles them better than anyone, which is the brother's entire vindication.
why.pressures: Both yards depend on the same hunters, who play them against each other every season, and the price of a live wamasu has doubled in five years.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would merge with the Charge Works within a year of either brother dying, and both families know it and nobody says it.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: near but not on a wamasu pond
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the only reason to live this close to that water
hardConstraints: a rock face to work against

notableNpcSlots: the brother who does lanterns
the hunter who sells to whichever yard bids higher

vibe.silhouette: An open yard against a rock face with racks of drying hide, a flushing channel, and a shed at the back glowing faintly blue after dark.

vibe.materials: Timber racks and a stone-lined flushing channel — the works is a plumbing arrangement with a shed attached.

vibe.condition: Well run, hard on its people, better equipped than its rival.
vibe.mood: Competent, bitter, and very good at one thing.
vibe.approach: The blue glow is the only night landmark on this channel and every boat navigates by it, including the rival's.
vibe.senses: Running water; hide being scraped; a hum from the shed that is not machinery.

provisions: organ lanterns: a light source with a supply chain and a feud attached
two works, one set of hunters, and a price nobody can control

places.name: The Monsoon Boom

why.founding: The Tear road's delta section goes under in the monsoon and Thorn closes it, because the alternative is losing caravans.
why.siteAdvantages: The lowest crossing of the terrace country, where the delta backs up first.
why.occupantsMotive: The barrier is worked by the paddy gate-holders, who are already there for the gates.
why.pressures: Dunmer caravans have twice ignored it and once been right, which is the whole problem.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be unnecessary if the road were embanked, and Thorn's owners will not pay for a road they do not own.

vibe.condition: Crude and functional.
vibe.approach: In the dry it is a chain lying in the dust; in the wet it is a boom on water with no road visible.
vibe.senses: Rain; the chain; water moving over a road surface.

places.name: Moon Court

why.founding: A roofless alchemical court where the apparatus is moved between fixed stations by moon phase — Stormhold's alchemists keep it outside the city because the work needs a clear sky and the city has lamps.
why.siteAdvantages: A dark upland flat with no light within four kilometres and a wall of rock to the north that kills the wind without blocking the sky.
why.occupantsMotive: Two resident alchemists and a rotation of Stormhold practitioners who book nights; the court's whole value is the darkness, which is a thing that can be spoiled and cannot be repaired.
why.pressures: Crystalgate's cutting sheds have begun burning lamps late and the court's northern sky is measurably worse than it was a decade ago.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be worthless the day anyone put a lit building on the ridge, and the alchemists have started buying land to prevent it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a settlement, above canopy where possible
hardConstraints: no artificial light within four kilometres
clear sky and a wind break
preferences: a ring of numbered stone stations

notableNpcSlots: the alchemist buying ridge land to stop a lamp
the Stormhold practitioner who books the dark nights

vibe.silhouette: A roofless walled court on a bare upland flat with a ring of stone stations around it and no roof, no lamp and no window.
vibe.palette: Stone grey by day; by night, no colour at all except the working fires, which are shielded on three sides.
vibe.materials: Dry stone and iron fittings, and apparatus that is carried rather than fixed — the building is a calendar and the equipment is furniture.
vibe.signatureFeature: The stations: a ring of numbered stone pads, and the apparatus stands on a different one each phase, so the court's plan is the lunar month.
vibe.condition: Well kept, deliberately unlit, and defended against light rather than against people.

vibe.senses: Shielded fire; something being ground very finely; complete darkness outside the court and complete darkness inside it.

a darkness that can be spoiled deliberately

lamp on the ridge (and the court's whole purpose in question)

places.name: Ninth Chapel

why.founding: An Imperial mission built a stone chapel on the north road and was dead of swamp fever inside a year; it was the ninth such attempt on this road and the numbering, which was the mission's own, is the only reason anyone remembers the other eight.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands on the only stone footing the mission could find, which is the corner of something much older that they did not investigate.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing. The north road passes it, and travellers shelter in it without any sense that they are in a chapel.
why.pressures: The roof is gone and the walls are sound; the Nisswo rest-house down the road treats it as a competitor that lost, and says so.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pulled down for its cut stone if the province had any use for cut stone, which it does not.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: far inland, where nobody wanted them
hardConstraints: a stone footing on the north road
preferences: a carved number over the door

vibe.approach: It is the only vertical stone on that stretch and reads from the road at half a kilometre.
vibe.senses: Wind through empty windows; rain on a floor with no roof; nothing devotional whatsoever.

provisions: eight earlier missions implied by one carved number — a chain to trace

places.name: North Post

why.founding: Argonia checks what comes down the Tear road, and what it is checking for is people being taken north.
why.siteAdvantages: Below the pass on the Argonian side, at the first point where a caravan can be stopped without being on a slope.
why.occupantsMotive: The keepers count heads out and heads back, a practice begun after the invasion and never repealed.
why.pressures: House Dres's successors find the count insulting; the keepers find that satisfying.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned if the Owing were ever abolished, because the Owing is what the count is really about.

vibe.senses: A tally called aloud; caravan noise; the rope being lowered.

places.name: North Cut

why.founding: An Imperial attempt to cut a hard road north from Stormhold to the Tear road, abandoned four kilometres in when the surveyors discovered what everyone local already knew about the sink.
why.siteAdvantages: It follows a line that looks correct on a map and is wrong on the ground, which is the whole province's Imperial history in one earthwork.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies it. The villages quarry the metalling for their own yards and consider this a form of restitution.
why.pressures: The cut has become a drainage channel it was never meant to be and is now actively rerouting water into ground that used to be dry.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a serious problem within a generation if the water it collects reached the plain villages, and one of them has started to notice.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the line of an abandoned Imperial road
hardConstraints: a straight engineered formation ending in sink

notableNpcSlots: the plain villager who has worked out where the water is going

vibe.silhouette: A dead-straight metalled cut running four kilometres into a sink and stopping, with the last hundred metres under water and a spoil bank alongside.
vibe.palette: Road-metal grey, sink black, and a hard green line of different vegetation along the spoil bank where the drainage has changed.
vibe.materials: Imperial road metal, quarried out in patches by whoever needed hardcore, over an engineered base that is still perfectly level.
vibe.signatureFeature: The stop: the road simply ends, mid-formation, with the next section's pegs still in the ground beyond the waterline.
vibe.condition: Level, sound, quarried, and doing something it was not designed to do.
vibe.mood: An expensive mistake, still working away at being a mistake.
vibe.approach: It is the straightest thing on the plain and you can see the whole of it at once from the spoil bank.
vibe.senses: Water running where it should not; boots on metalled surface, then on mud, then nothing.

provisions: a piece of infrastructure quietly causing a flood nobody has connected to it yet

localStateVariants: dry season (the pegs visible)
wet season (a kilometre of it under water, and the drainage obvious)

places.name: The Waiting Hole

why.founding: Thorn's field-owners need somewhere to put a debtor between the field and the court, and will not build a gaol because Argonians do not.

why.pressures: The Freed Rows keep a tally of who goes in and who comes out, and the counts do not always match.

why.pressures: Both cities have tried to buy an exception; the refusals are part of the family's standing.

places.name: The Cold Gallery

why.founding: The root layer reaches its northern limit here, and where it thins over cold rim ground it leaves galleries that are colder and drier than any in the south.
why.siteAdvantages: Between the swamp's edge and the rim's stone, where roots run over rock instead of mud.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing keeps it; the prospectors' camp above uses the first chamber as a store.
why.pressures: It is the only root gallery in the province with a stone floor, which makes it navigable and makes it dangerous differently.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the north's cave system if anyone mapped it, and the prospectors have started to.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect, and that connection is the map
hardConstraints: roots over rock rather than mud

vibe.palette: Root brown above, grey stone below, and a cold blue light at two collapses.
vibe.materials: No construction; the prospectors' store boxes are the only made objects.
vibe.signatureFeature: The floor: dry stone under a wet ceiling, so it drips continuously onto rock and the sound never stops.
vibe.condition: The upper chambers stable; the lower ones changing as roots shift.
vibe.mood: Cold, echoing, unlike the rest of the province underground.
vibe.approach: The mouth is behind the prospectors' camp and looks like a store, which it partly is.
vibe.senses: Dripping onto stone with a hard echo; roots creaking; a draught from deeper in.

why.siteAdvantages: A ridge nose above the Tear road, high enough to clear the haze on a cold morning.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it; couriers use it to check the weather and travellers climb it for the reason anyone climbs anything.
why.pressures: It is the one place from which the province's scale is legible, and almost nobody in the province has been there.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not change, and does not need to.

vibe.materials: One cairn. Nothing else, and nothing else is wanted.

vibe.condition: Unchanged except by the cairn growing.

vibe.senses: Wind; nothing else; the marsh is too far away to be heard, which is itself extraordinary.

places.name: Northern Rest

why.occupantsMotive: It is maintained by villages who would not describe themselves as devout and would be offended to be called otherwise.
why.pressures: No Nisswo has come for three years, and the house is still swept weekly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be maintained anyway. That is the whole point of the institution.

why.pressures: Greylight has asked twice for it to be cleared and Stormhold has not answered.

places.name: Shell Ground

why.founding: Armoured shell-beasts work a stretch of gravel bar for the molluscs in it, and where they work, they moult — which makes this the region's raw material source for shell plate, and one of the more dangerous places to stand in the north.

why.wouldChangeIf: Would stop producing entirely if the mollusc bed were over-taken, which the gatherers police far more strictly than they police the timing.

places.name: White Pans

why.founding: Hissmir's Trials cannot take everyone at once, so the overflow camps on the last dry ground before the village and waits — sometimes for a week, occasionally for a season.
why.siteAdvantages: The last firm ground on the pilgrim path, with water, wood and a view of the village that is close enough to be maddening.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilgrims, most of them Hist-less, all of them unwilling to go home; the camp organises itself into an order of arrival that the Root Stewards do not recognise and everybody obeys.
why.pressures: The waiting order is the camp's only law and it is enforced by people with nothing else left, which occasionally goes badly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty overnight if the Stewards ever refused a comer, which canon says they cannot, which is precisely why the camp keeps growing.

why.founding: Five houses that went into the ground over about a decade as the peat beneath them compacted, slowly enough that the households kept re-levelling floors until the doors would no longer open.
why.siteAdvantages: It was, when it was built, the best-drained ground in the district — because it was drying peat, which is exactly why it sank.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody, now. The last household left with the roof still on and the walls at eleven degrees.
why.pressures: The subsidence has not stopped; the site is measurably lower each decade and the hollow now holds water for half the year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a pond within two generations, and the villages nearby have stopped using the name.

places.name: Wolk Market
sources: uesp:Lore:Ten-Maur-Wolk (the junction and the Imperial renaming; the town is ours)

why.founding: A market grew where the roads from Helstrom, Stormhold and Alten Corimont converge — the only three-way road hinge in the north. It takes its name from the ruin beside it, shortened, because nobody wanted to name a town after Boethiah and nobody could avoid the landmark either.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground at the convergence, above the flooding that closes the roads either side of it for two months a year, with spring water enough for a market but not enough to tempt anyone to build a port here.
why.occupantsMotive: It exists to take a cut of everything moving between the interior, the border city and the smugglers' port, and to be the place where three sets of weights are argued into one.
why.pressures: Prosperous, indefensible, and next door to a Daedric ruin it will not discuss; Stormhold's vicecanons want its market fees and Alten Corimont's brokers want its warehousing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be fought over the week any of the three roads mattered militarily, and would have to build the fourth wall it has never had.
